title: Customer Alignment 60m Engagement Script and Ops Checklist
content:
Purpose and positioning:
This is a compact, facilitator-first runbook for a 60‑minute customer alignment sprint that functions as a lightweight QBR. It is designed for mid‑market accounts where we want to drive a focused set of decisions (renewal posture, adoption milestones, prioritized action items) without a long exec briefing. Use this when customer signals show mixed usage but strong strategic potential.

Meeting objective (one sentence):
Leave with a clear renewal posture and three prioritized, owner‑assigned actions that materially reduce churn risk in the next 30–60 days.

Top three success criteria (measurable):
- Stakeholder alignment: at least one exec sponsor commits to the top action by end of meeting.
- Operational clarity: owners, due dates, and success metrics assigned for 3 actions.
- Risk delta: at least one technical or adoption blocker moved from "unknown" to "triaged with ETA".

Pre-read (send 72h before):
- 1‑page adoption snapshot (active seats, daily active users, top 5 APIs by volume, 30/60/90d trend).
- Cost/latency trend: 90d token spend and p50/p95 latency chart.
- Open risk log (short bullets).
- Draft recommendation: our preferred ask and fallback options.

Attendee guide (who should join):
- Customer: Primary product owner, engineering lead or platform owner, executive sponsor (optional but preferred).
- Redwood: CSM (facilitator), Solutions Engineer (technical SME), Account Executive (renewal owner - optional for exec ask).

Roles during the meeting (brief):
- Facilitator (CSM) — timebox, keep decisions on track, summarize commitments.
- Tech SME — answer technical clarifications, own follow-up tech actions.
- Note taker — capture decisions and action owners (can be the CSM if small meeting).

Agenda (60 minutes total):
0–5m — Quick check-in + meeting objective: set the stage, confirm desired outcomes.
5–15m — Customer highlight reel: customer shares 2 wins and 1 pain. Keep it tight.
15–28m — Adoption & metrics deep dive: walk pre-read highlights, focus on delta signals (what changed).
28–38m — Risk ladder + root cause mapping: identify top 2 risks and map to root cause (people/process/tech).
38–50m — Proposed asks & options: present 1 primary ask (what we want them to commit to) and 2 fallback options; elicit feedback.
50–58m — Commitments and success metrics: capture owners, due dates, and how we will measure success.
58–60m — Close: next steps, schedule check-in cadence, and any parking‑lot items.

Facilitation script (concise prompts and cues):
- 0–5m opener: "Thanks all — our aim is to leave with three concrete actions and a clear renewal posture. If we do that, we’ve been successful. Quick round: one win and one sticking point from your side?"
- If exec not present: ask early for a timeline and who will sign off on the top ask; propose scheduling a 15m follow-up with the exec.
- During metrics section: use data to force a choice. Prompt: "Given the 23% downtrend in daily inference volume, which of these causes feels most plausible to your team?" Provide multiple choice options (implementation, cost, UX, competing priorities).
- Risk ladder mapping: visually stack impact x probability; ask customer to place each risk in the matrix. Use this to prioritize remediation.
- Present ask framing: "If we could resolve X in 30 days, we expect Y impact on adoption and Z on cost — would you be willing to commit resource A to achieve that?"
- Closing: read back three actions, ask for explicit agreement: "Do you agree these are the right priorities and owners?"

Suggested primary ask templates (pick one and customize):
- Product integration ask: "Assign an engineer for a 2‑week spike to enable prefix caching; expected lift: +15–20% throughput with no code changes. Can you allocate one engineer for weeks 2–3?"
- Adoption outreach ask: "Commit to a 6‑email targeted play to top 25 users over 30 days; we’ll provide copy and tracking — can you own execution?"
- Exec ask for renewal: "We’d like an early renewal decision (signed LOI) with a scoped pilot extension to run through Q2 to de‑risk performance goals — can we confirm a week for final decision?"

Decision ladder (simple text matrix for facilitator):
- Green: proceed to renew now with support plan; owners assigned.
- Yellow: conditional renewal pending completion of 1–2 technical actions (list actions and dates).
- Red: pause negotiations — require follow-up pilot or technical remediation before renewal.

Risk signals to surface during the meeting (quick checklist):
- Sustained downward trend in DAU or API calls > 14 days.
- New error class or rising p95 latency > target.
- Key user churn (top 10 users by activity) in last 30 days.
- Unresolved security/compliance asks on critical path to renewal.
- Escalation backlog > 3 priority incidents in 60 days.

Data pull checklist (ops prep — run before meeting):
- Last 90 days: daily token usage, active user counts, top endpoints by volume.
- Performance: p50/p95 latency, error rate, time-of-day heatmap.
- Cost snapshot: 30/60/90d spend by environment and top 5 expensive prompts.
- Support: open tickets, SLA misses, major incidents with resolution notes.
- Billing: upcoming invoices, credits, and any disputed charges.

Parking lot and escalation lanes (how to handle off‑topics):
- Add non‑urgent roadmap asks to the parking lot and commit to a 5‑min follow-up note within 48h.
- If an escalation is raised that threatens production, pause the agenda and trigger an internal war‑room (CS + SE + SRE) within 2 business hours.

Post‑meeting follow-up templates (send within 24 hours):
- Summary email subject: "[Company] + Redwood: 60m Alignment — Decisions & Next Steps"
- Body bullets: meeting purpose, three decisions, owners + due dates, success metrics, scheduled check-in date, parking lot items, and links to artifacts.

Action tracker sprint table (one line per action — use in follow-up):
- Action title | Owner | Due date | Success metric | Status | Notes
- Example: "Enable prefix cache spike" | Omar Khan | 2025‑02‑10 | +15% throughput p50 | in_progress | kickoff scheduled 2025‑01‑22

Escalation rubric (if action falls behind):
- Missed milestone without update > 3 business days: CSM sends 1st escalation to owner + manager.
- Missed milestone > 7 days or blocker is critical: schedule a remediation triage and loop in AE for contractual implications.

Meeting artifacts (deliverables to attach to follow-up):
- Adoption snapshot (PDF)
- Action tracker (sheet link)
- Technical remediation plan (if applicable)
- Proposed renewal/options summary (1‑pager)

Ops-level preflight checklist (30–60 minutes of prep):
- Confirm pre-read sent and opened by customer.
- Validate data pulls: charts render, numbers reconcile with billing.
- Confirm attendee list and exec availability.
- Prepare 1‑page decision summary slide.
- SE: rehearse answers for top 3 technical objections.
- CSM: prepare follow-up calendar invites for the cadence you propose.

Tips for difficult conversations and common objections:
- If customer says "we don’t have bandwidth": offer a smaller, staged ask and a Redwood‑owned pilot with success criteria.
- If customer pushes for lower price: reframe to focus on unit economics — identify which model or route reduces cost per inference and make a technical recommendation.
- If exec requests more data: propose a 15‑day pilot with metric gating and commit to a daily or twice‑weekly readout.

Template closing readout (what facilitator says):
"To summarize: we agreed on X (owner, due date), Y (owner, due date), Z (owner, due date). Our renewal posture is [Green/Yellow/Red] with the following conditions. I will send the follow-up with the tracker within 24 hours and schedule the 30‑day check‑in for [date]. Thanks everyone — anything else before we close?"

Notes to CSM after the meeting (internal):
- Immediately update action tracker and ping owners in Slack with the one‑line ask and link to tracker.
- If posture is Yellow/Red, draft a short risk brief for the CSM manager and AE with recommended mitigations and proposed timeline for remediation.

Quick heuristics for renewal posture (to use if time-constrained):
- Green if: DAU stable or up, top 3 blockers triaged, exec sponsor engaged.
- Yellow if: one high‑impact action outstanding with owner identified.
- Red if: two or more unresolved technical blockers, no exec sponsor, or critical compliance gaps.

Appendix: quick scripts for calendar invites and pre-reads:
- Invite subject: "60m Alignment: [Customer] x Redwood — Outcomes, Risks, & Next Steps"
- Pre-read blurb in invite: "Please read the attached 1‑page adoption snapshot before the meeting. We’ll run a 60‑minute alignment sprint and aim to leave with three prioritized actions and a recommended renewal posture."

End of document.
